sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The stolen bride is a bride taken by the fairies. The stories about her belong to the wide tale of Fairy Kidnapping. A woman leaves her home in her bridal wear and falls into a sleep she cannot wake. The fairies have taken her spirit into their world. The man who is to marry her must find the fairy mound and bring her back. Even then the bride may carry a trace from the fairy world. A pin or a thread of fairyland may stay on her clothes. To wake her, one must find that fine thread and draw it out. The stolen bride is most at risk at the moment of marriage. Brides stand near the top of the list of those the fairies might take.
